title: Given the area or volume, find a dimension
subtitle: Area and volume · 24 official questions

sections.heading: Where this sits for you
body: **24 of the official questions in Area and volume are this one** — 9 Easy, 11 Medium, 4 Hard.
It is bottom-heavy, which makes it cheap points. Secure it early.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:
- The area or volume is already given as a number, and the question asks for a missing length: a base, an edge, a radius or a labelled variable on a figure.

sections.heading: The method
body: - 1) Write the formula and set it equal to the given area or volume.
- 3) Isolate the unknown: divide, then take a square root if the unknown is squared, and keep only the positive root.

sections.heading: Where Desmos fits
body: Type the formula as an equation in x, for example (1/3)π(3)² x = 473 or 8x² = 1152, and read off the x-intercept or intersection.
This removes the algebra, including the square root.

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: You may forget the ½ or ⅓ when you undo the formula, or stop before taking the square root.
In a triangle, you may divide the area by the height without doubling it first.
